patient.chief_complaint: Two years of asymmetric leg pain and weakness, worse on the left, with recent right foot drop
patient.history_present_illness: Lena Marchetti is a 51-year-old schoolteacher presenting with a 2-year history of progressive and strikingly asymmetric lower extremity symptoms. The illness began with severe burning pain in her left calf and thigh, initially attributed to lumbar radiculopathy by her primary care physician. An MRI lumbar spine 18 months ago showed moderate L3-L4 and L4-L5 stenosis, and she underwent two epidural steroid injections without sustained benefit. Over the subsequent year, she developed right foot drop with steppage gait on the right, which was abrupt in onset over 3 days. Her left leg pain persists but has partly improved. She also notes intermittent right hand clumsiness and occasional elbow area pain on the right. There is no classic glove-and-stocking numbness. She denies bowel or bladder dysfunction. Her diabetes was diagnosed 6 months ago during workup for this presentation — HbA1c was 6.9%. She has lost 8 kg over the past year without trying, which she initially attributed to reduced appetite from pain. She denies fever, rash, oral ulcers, or joint swelling. Past medical history includes a remote episode of pleuritis 8 years ago, attributed to 'viral illness' at the time but never formally evaluated. She takes no immunosuppressants. Her symptoms and the asymmetric stepwise pattern have been puzzling to her treating physicians.

specialized_test.impression: ABNORMAL NCS/EMG — mononeuritis multiplex pattern. Stepwise asymmetric axonal injury: right peroneal (amplitude severely reduced, acute denervation on EMG), left tibial and peroneal (subacute, moderate amplitude reduction), right ulnar (mild amplitude reduction). Amplitude-predominant loss without significant slowing, consistent with axonal degeneration. No conduction block. Pattern localizes to multiple individual peripheral nerves in an asymmetric, non-length-dependent distribution

output.impression: Epineurial vessel wall inflammation with transmural neutrophilic infiltrate and fibrinoid necrosis. Axonal degeneration in multiple fascicles. Findings of an epineurial vasculitic process; the underlying systemic association requires clinical and serologic correlation.
Minor salivary gland biopsy: focus score 2 foci/4 mm². Lymphocytic sialadenitis confirmed. Findings consistent with primary Sjögren's syndrome.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Sjögren's syndrome-associated vasculitic peripheral neuropathy (mononeuritis multiplex)

differential.key_features: Identical multifocal axonal pattern; need ANCA, eosinophil count, sinus/lung review.
Similar mononeuritis multiplex; need cryoglobulins, complement, hepatitis C serology.
Newly diagnosed T2DM HbA1c 6.9% is mild; pure asymmetric mononeuritis multiplex of named nerves is more vasculitic than diabetic.
Pre-existing L3-L4 / L4-L5 stenosis is a distractor; sensory + motor deficits in named peripheral nerve territories (not myotomes/dermatomes) are not radicular.
CIDP is symmetric and demyelinating; this case is asymmetric multifocal axonal — not CIDP.

optimal_actions.action: Order broad neuropathy labs (CBC, CMP, HbA1c, B12 + MMA, TSH, SPEP/IFE, urinalysis)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify reversible/treatable etiologies (diabetes, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, thyroid disease)

optimal_actions.action: Order EMG/NCS to characterize axonal vs demyelinating pattern and distribution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Length-dependent axonal vs demyelinating vs multifocal pattern; severity and distribution

optimal_actions.action: Search literature for DSP evaluation guidelines and etiology-specific recommendations
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm AAN 2009 DSP workup, etiology-specific evaluations

optimal_actions.action: Review medications for neurotoxic agents and check interactions for symptomatic therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify potentially neurotoxic drugs (chemotherapy, metronidazole, megadose B6, nitrofurantoin); guide neuropathic-pain pharmacotherapy

optimal_actions.action: Vasculitis + paraneoplastic panel (ANA, ANCA, ESR/CRP, RF, complement, anti-Hu/CV2/PNMA, cryoglobulins)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify vasculitic or paraneoplastic etiology in asymmetric/mononeuritis-multiplex pattern

optimal_actions.action: Sural nerve biopsy when vasculitic / mononeuritis multiplex / amyloid suspected
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Necrotizing vasculitis or amyloid deposition or demyelination/onion-bulbs (CIDP) on histopathology

optimal_actions.action: Sjögren's serology (anti-SSA / anti-SSB) and minor salivary gland (lip) biopsy if seronegative with sicca features
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anti-SSA/SSB or focal lymphocytic sialadenitis (focus score ≥1) supports Sjögren's syndrome

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Advanced cerebral imaging (PET/MRA/MRV/perfusion) has no routine role in peripheral neuropathy.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.
EMG/NCS localizes and characterizes lesion before nerve biopsy, guiding which nerve to biopsy and aiding interpretation.

critical_actions: Recognize mononeuritis multiplex pattern (asymmetric, multifocal, individual named-nerve deficits)
Obtain ANCA, ANA/ENA (including anti-SSA/SSB), ESR/CRP, complement, cryoglobulins, hepatitis serologies
Sural / superficial peroneal nerve biopsy to confirm necrotizing vasculitis
Initiate immunosuppression (high-dose corticosteroids ± cyclophosphamide / rituximab) after biopsy confirmation
contraindicated_actions: Do not ascribe to diabetic neuropathy without addressing the asymmetric multifocal pattern
Do not delay immunosuppression once vasculitic neuropathy is confirmed — axonal damage is time-dependent
Do not start chronic NSAIDs without renal/GI risk assessment in a patient on immunosuppression workup
key_reasoning_points: Asymmetric multifocal motor and sensory deficits = mononeuritis multiplex (vasculitis until proven otherwise)
Newly-diagnosed T2DM (HbA1c 6.9%) and lumbar stenosis are red herrings that explain neither the asymmetry nor the systemic features
Nerve biopsy of an affected, accessible nerve is the gold standard; necrotizing vasculitis confirms diagnosis
Sjögren's is a common underlying connective tissue cause of vasculitic neuropathy in middle-aged women

red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on diabetic neuropathy and miss vasculitic etiology
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Mild new-onset diabetes does not produce mononeuritis multiplex.

red_herrings.data_point: Lumbar spondylosis L3-L4 / L4-L5 with prior epidural steroid injections
red_herrings.intended_effect: Bias toward radicular explanation for the leg deficits
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Deficits follow individual peripheral nerves, not dermatomal/myotomal patterns; spondylosis is incidental.
